posts.name: Marc Mueller
posts.cooked:
Building on the ideas from PEP 505 and after many discussions over the years, I’m happy to present PEP 824: None-coalescing operators. Please be sure to also check out the discussion for the companion PEP 823.

Abstract

This PEP proposes adding two new operators.

  • The “None-coalescing” operator ??
  • The “None-coalescing assignment” operator ??=

The general idea is to provide a conditional operator, similar to or, which instead of truthiness, checks for None values.

The “None-coalescing” operator evaluates the left-hand side, checks whether it is not None, and if not, returns the result. If the value is None, the right-hand side is evaluated and returned.

The “None-coalescing assignment” operator will only assign the right-hand side to the left-hand side if the left-hand side evaluates to None.

They are roughly equivalent to:

# a ?? b
_t if ((_t := a) is not None) else b

# a ??= b
if a is None:
    a = b

–
An interactive demo is available here: https://pep823-and-pep824-demo.pages.dev/

Python Enhancement Proposals (PEPs)

posts.name: Xiaowei Lu
posts.cooked: I think using ??= is a good idea. When I write code, I don’t use conditional expressions very often, for the reasons the PEP describes. In the code I work on, the difference between age = user.age ?? "unknown" and age = user.age or "unknown" feels small, since 0 is usually not a value I need to keep. That’s only my own experience, though. Using ?? does make the check more precise, because it filters out only None.

posts.name: Michael H
posts.cooked:
Of the pair of proposals, I’m more enthusiastically positive about this one. I’m glad to see the intentional limiting of both to handling exactly None.

Changing the existing None checks I have where 824 could be used is not something that would push me to upgrade minimum python versions any faster, but it is a real improvement and may help prevent people from using or when there is a potential falsey value they had not considered.

posts.name: Chris Markiewicz
posts.cooked:
I would be very glad to see this accepted, and I am also glad to see it limited to exactly None. Extending to sentinels or other objects would replicate the pitfalls of __bool__.

Just a note on the precedence:

# x or y ?? 2
(x or y) ?? 2

# "Hello" if x ?? True else 0
"Hello" if (x ?? True) else 0

and

Furthermore, setting the precedence between or and conditional expressions matches other languages which have implemented the operator, like JS [8] and C# [10].

This is correct, but the JS and C# examples are interesting in that x || y ?? 2 is a type error in C# and a syntax error in JS. It may be worth exploring whether other languages permit intermixing with boolean operators, or if Python would be unique in this respect.

That said, I find the JS behavior surprising and annoying, so agree with the current design that parentheses should remain optional when precedence matches intent.

posts.name: tushar c.

Thank you for putting this PEP together. I support this. I think PEP 824 is clearer than earlier versions like PEP 505. I think splitting this + PEP 823 was a good idea. Like others in this thread, I appreciate the intentional decision to only handle None and not anything false-y.

posts.name: Boss_1s
posts.cooked:
What if both Coalesce operators had their own dunder methods to change the check/assignment for None to something else like a custom Sentinel object? Would that be redundant or overly confusing?

Something like:

class Foo:
    MISSING = sentinel("MISSING")

    def __init__(self, bar=MISSING) -> None:
        self.bar = bar

    def __cgetattribute__(self, name, fallback): # ??
        # None-coalescing becomes MISSING-coalescing
        return fallback ?? self.name

    def __csetattr__(self, name, value): # ??=
        # None-coalescing assignment becomes MISSING-coalescing assignment
        if self.__cgetattribute__(self, name) is MISSING:
            super().__setattr__(name, value)

obj = Foo()

obj.bar ?? "unknown" # Returns "unknown"

obj.bar ??= "bax" # obj.bar is now "bax"
obj.bar ??= "baq" # obj.bar is still "bax"

obj.bar ?? "unknown" # Returns "bax"

(This example can be improved on)

posts.name: Monarch
posts.cooked: Massive +1. I’ve written libraries for dealing with APIs with hundreds of nested fields, most of them optional, and I’ve spent a lot of time making sure the user only has to deal with typed objects that are nice to work with in Python. posts.name: Marc Mueller
posts.cooked:
My bad. Almost all languages with coalescing operators use ?? and ??=. AFAIR all prior discussions, including PEP 505, used them as well.

Why ?? and not a single ?: The None-coalescing operator is a conditional operator. As such it’s more closely related to and / or than binary operators +, -, &, |, … Looking at other languages again, and is often spelled as &&, or as ||. Both use two chars to differentiate them from their binary counterparts.

+1 from me, I was very excited to see this idea get revitalized as a new PEP.

People suggesting other syntax options should also explain why this feature should use anything else but the notation that is already widely used in a dozen of other major languages. posts.name: Steve Dower
posts.cooked:
The ?? syntax has a very natural pairing with ?., and since they are two parts of what should usually be the same expression, it makes sense for both to have some level of consistency.[1]

By “natural pairing” I mean that a?.b ?? c should be a typical usage, where None is only really a special intermediate value and not an intentional result. Translated into current code, this would be a.b if a is not None and a.b is not None else c[2]. Both expressions are pretty good in this respect - the former uses punctuation operators and the latter using textual operators, and the precedence works as each naturally reads.[3]

  1. It’s irrelevant since I’ve withdrawn my own efforts on this, but I wouldn’t have split the PEP up into two. The value of ?? is strongest when ?. exists, and with either half of the syntax missing, the value quickly becomes zero or negative. ↩︎

  2. Without the repeated evaluations, of course. ↩︎

  3. Though, of course, I don’t prefer either syntax over a traversal helper function or a data model that simply doesn’t allow Nones to reach my business logic. ↩︎
